name: Barney
lede: Barney is a vivid magenta-purple named for a person: our data records it only as "named for a person: barney," the kind of instant color comparison the 2010 xkcd survey's crowd reached for on sight.

sections.title: A person's name for a color everyone recognizes
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Our data classifies it as a person-tier name but does not resolve which Barney respondents had in mind [1]. Pop culture's best-known Barney is the purple children's television dinosaur, though the survey record does not confirm that link [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a vivid purple, about 5.6 units off, with Munsell notation 7.1P 4.3/19.2 [1].

A closely related entry, [[dark-magenta|Barney Purple]], names a duller and darker variant from the same vote, 5.8 units away [1]. The nearest other look-alikes in our data are [[purple-munsell|Purple-Munsell]], more vivid, [[purple-plum|Purply]], a duller neighbor, and [[dark-orchid|Dark Orchid]], purpler [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 difference of 4, as photographed [2]. A magenta-purple this saturated has no real match among historical pigments, which painters could rarely mix this bright and this cool at once [2].
